newsitem.title: USA: WMX to divest $1.5 bln assets, cut budget.
newsitem.headline: WMX to divest $1.5 bln assets, cut budget.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc said Tuesday it would divest non-core and non-integrated assets valued at about $1.5 billion to focus on its waste management services business.

WMX said the divestments, to take place in the next 18 to 24 months, were part of a comprehensive change in business strategy that should generate $3 billion in free cash after dividends over the next two years.
WMX said the plan includes cutting its capital budget for 1997 to $900 million, from $1.1 billion in 1996.
"We will add value by concentrating on the basics of the waste management services business," the company said in a release.

Under the plan, WMX's Wheelabrator Technologies Inc subsidiary will sell its remaining water services for $77 million, and WMX's Rust International Inc unit will sell its remaininng engineering and consulting businesses.

Also, WMX will sell about $400 million of non-integrated waste services business in North America and cut its investment in all or parts of its businesses in France, Spain and Austria through joint ventures or sales.

WMX said it will save about $300 million over the next two to three years through initiatives that include cutting 1,200 jobs in 1997 and cutting a total of 3,000 jobs over the next two to three years. The job cuts will be done through attrition, early retirement and layoffs, it said.
Including jobs eliminated with its discontinued businesses, WMX will employ fewer than 58,000 workers in 1997, down from about 73,000 at the beginning of 1996, the company said.
WMX also said it would change its name back to Waste Management Inc.
